a single mutation in the PhoQ kinase of Salmonella enterica results in a dramatic change in the phenotype of this bacterium, from a graded to a bistable response.
a single mutation can have a profound impact on a signaling network.
a single point mutant of the Pho Q protein in E. coli, which is a sensor kinase in a two-component signal transduction system, results in a bistable response to stimulus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a prototypical bacterial signaling circuit can be re-wired to have a novel property by a single point mutation.
the PhoQ phosphatase domain is not necessary for PhoQ to function as a signaling protein, but it is essential for PhoQ/ PhoP to function as a two-component system.
a single point mutant of the PhoP/PhoQ system can cause dramatic changes in the system properties, and that this is due to the particular architecture of the PhoPh/PhoQ signaling network.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple change in a protein can have dramatic consequences in a network.
the PhoQ protein is a versatile signaling component that can be adapted to perform a variety of signaling functions.
even a single point mutation can cause a qualitative change in the function of a network, and the architecture of a network can determine how a point mutation will affect its function.
